step_by_step_reasoning: The logical architecture represents Cinefilm's PixelStrings platform on AWS. First, a user connects via a Web Browser to the WEB SERVER / JOB MANAGER running on an Amazon EC2 instance. The user provides keys to their Amazon S3 bucket. To dynamically display metadata in the browser, the Job Manager invokes an AWS Lambda function which extracts metadata from media files in S3 and caches it in an Amazon RDS Database. For processing jobs, the Job Manager controls the G3 / A.M. (Asset Manager) EC2 instances. The Asset Manager copies files from the user's S3 bucket to local storage on G3 instances, which run GPU-accelerated video enhancement jobs (wormhole, spacetime, dark energy). Once complete, the Asset Manager copies the output back to S3. If IMF is chosen, the output is routed to an IMF EC2 instance for packaging before final upload to S3.

graph.name: Cinefilm PixelStrings Media Processing Architecture
graph.categories: Media Processing, GPU Acceleration, Serverless Metadata Extraction
graph.notes: PixelStrings is a cloud-based media conversion and optimization platform utilizing GPU-accelerated G3 EC2 instances, AWS Lambda for asynchronous metadata extraction, and Amazon RDS for caching.

nodes.name: Web Browser
nodes.notes: User interacts with the PixelStrings web interface, typically via Chrome, to log in and manage workflows.

nodes.name: WEB SERVER / JOB MANAGER
nodes.notes: EC2 instance running the web front-end and the core job manager that orchestrates metadata and processing workflows.

nodes.name: DATABASE
nodes.notes: Relational database used to store and cache extracted media metadata so the Web Server can display it quickly.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Customer's own S3 bucket containing the input raw video clips and receiving the processed outputs.

nodes.name: LAMBDA
nodes.notes: AWS Lambda function used to asynchronously extract video and photo metadata directly from files in S3.

nodes.name: G3 / A.M.
nodes.notes: GPU-accelerated EC2 cluster running Cinefilm processing tools and an Asset Manager (A.M.) to handle file transfers.

nodes.name: IMF
nodes.notes: Interoperable Master Format wrapping server running on EC2 to package video outputs specifically for distribution channels like Netflix.

edges.notes: User logs into the Web Server and inputs S3 credentials/keys.
Job Manager triggers AWS Lambda to fetch file metadata from the user's S3 bucket.
Lambda reads file headers from the customer's S3 bucket to extract metadata.
Lambda returns the extracted media metadata to the Job Manager.
Job Manager saves and caches the metadata in the database.
Web Server retrieves the cached metadata from the database to present to the user's browser.
Job Manager submits processing jobs to the G3 EC2 cluster and commands Asset Manager to copy clips.
Asset Manager copies the input video clip from the user's S3 bucket to the G3 instance's local storage.
G3 instance processes the video using GPU acceleration (e.g., retiming, de-interlacing).
Asset Manager copies the final processed output clip back to the user's S3 bucket.
Job Manager starts an IMF packaging workflow on the G3 cluster.
Asset Manager copies raw input files to the processing cluster.
Processed output is sent to the IMF wrapping component for standard-compliant packaging.
Asset Manager uploads the packaged IMF output package back to the user's S3 bucket.
